lead.headline: Kauaʻi recovery reaches 82% power restoration as schools and transit resume
lead.summary: County officials say about 82% of KIUC members have power again while most schools and regular bus service prepare to resume Monday.
lead.why_it_matters: Families and workers need the latest school, transit, water and facility guidance as recovery progresses unevenly across the island.
body: Kauaʻi’s recovery from Hurricane Lowell continued Sunday, with power restored to about 82% of Kauaʻi Island Utility Cooperative members, according to a September 13 County of Kauaʻi update. Roughly 7,000 members remained without service, and 13 of the island’s 15 transmission lines had been restored.

The county said about 250 personnel were deployed in the response. Boil-water notices for Kīlauea and Wainiha-Hāʻena had been lifted, but residents were still being asked to conserve water islandwide while systems recovered.

Regular Kauaʻi Bus and paratransit service is scheduled to resume Monday, September 14. Routes 900 and 950 will remain suspended for the week, so riders should check current county transit notices before traveling.

Nearly all public schools are expected to reopen Monday. Hanalei and Kīlauea elementary schools are to remain closed through at least September 14, with a target of September 15, while Chiefess Kamakahelei Middle School is scheduled to reopen September 15.

Recovery restrictions remain in place. The Līhuʻe Civic Center, county parks and campgrounds, and Wailua Golf Course remain closed; a brown-water advisory continues. Travelers, residents and families should use the county’s official update for the latest road, food-distribution and facility details because conditions may change.

stories.headline: Lifeline Awareness Week highlights help with phone and internet costs
stories.summary: The Hawaiʻi Public Utilities Commission is directing qualifying households to the federal Lifeline program during September 13–19.
stories.why_it_matters: Reliable phone and internet access can connect residents with emergency services, health care, work, school and family resources.
body: Hawaiʻi’s Public Utilities Commission is using National Digital Connectivity and Lifeline Awareness Week, September 13–19, to remind residents about a federal program that can reduce qualifying phone and internet costs.

The Federal Communications Commission’s Lifeline program offers eligible households a monthly discount of up to $9.25 for qualifying internet or bundled phone-and-internet service, or up to $5.25 for voice-only phone service, according to the PUC.
Eligibility generally depends on household income or participation in certain federal assistance programs. The PUC does not process applications or decide whether an individual qualifies.

Residents can review complete eligibility requirements, apply and locate participating providers through LifelineSupport.org. The Lifeline Support Center is also available at 1-800-234-9473 for questions about eligibility, applications or an existing benefit.

The program is intended to make essential communications more affordable for qualifying households. Applicants should rely on the official Lifeline site for current requirements and should not send personal eligibility information to PinoyLink.
